marrow__BIOCHEM_CH18_Q017.explanation:
Chymotrypsinogen is a zymogen. Its active form, chymotrypsin, is a serine protease.

Serine proteases are proteolytic enzymes having serine, histidine and aspartate at the active site. The active site consists of two binding sites and a catalytic site. While serine is present in the catalytic site of serine proteases, histidine and aspartate are present on binding sites. Serine proteases differ in substrate specificity.

Examples of serine proteases:
• Chymotrypsin
• Trypsin
• Elastase
• Thrombin
• Plasmin
• Complements
• Factor X and XI
• Prostate-specific antigen
